without_term.text: What are the latest deep learning techniques and models being used in image analysis for corrosion detection, classification and segmentation
without_term.answer:
# Overview: Tasks, Data, and Problem Setups

Corrosion image analysis typically combines three related tasks: binary or component-level detection/localization, pixel-wise segmentation, and classification of corrosion type or severity, applied to field photographs, bridge components, cargo containers, or high-resolution microscopy images. <cite id="54189cdc-4">Recent overviews describe end-to-end pipelines that integrate deep learning segmentation with detection/classification for pitting corrosion on steel structures</cite>. <cite id="54189cdc-0">High-magnification SEM images are now commonly used to train segmentation models that capture fine-scale corrosion boundaries and morphology</cite>. <cite id="54189cdc-3">Industrial inspection use-cases emphasize real-time or near-real-time systems for container inspection, where deep-learning vision improves throughput and defect sensitivity</cite>.

# Pixel-wise Segmentation: CNNs, Transformers, and Hybrid Designs

Modern segmentation favors lightweight transformer backbones and hybrid CNN–Transformer architectures, often with encoder–decoder structures. <cite id="54189cdc-2">SegFormer-based models deliver near-real-time rust segmentation by replacing heavy convolutional stacks with lightweight token-mixing layers, enabling deployment on resource-constrained inspection hardware</cite>. <cite id="54189cdc-8">Transformer segmenters have been adapted explicitly to metal corrosion, addressing the difficulty of accurately delineating small and irregular corrosion foci; improved token aggregation and boundary-sensitive losses significantly raise IoU over standard CNN baselines in ablations</cite>. <cite id="54189cdc-4">Empirical comparisons show encoder–decoder CNNs (e.g., UNet/UNet++) remain competitive when encoder depth and feature pyramid design are tuned for corrosion textures, with training schedules and data augmentation playing a major role</cite>.

Transformer-centric methods are also emerging for structural-scale segmentation. <cite id="536e62dc-4">On industrial equipment, transformer-based architectures improved mean IoU by 4.9–6.2% over convolutional segmenters, demonstrating the benefit of self-attention for long-range feature fusion in complex surface defects, a trend increasingly applied in corrosion domains</cite>. <cite id="536e62dc-1">Steel-bridge-specific segmentation datasets (e.g., 514 images spanning multiple severity levels) are paired with advanced training losses such as Distance-IoU to improve segmentation accuracy and regression of bounding box masks in two-stage frameworks</cite>.

Beyond pixel segmentation, multi-task architectures integrate detection and rating. <cite id="54189cdc-5">Unified multi-task frameworks combine learned preprocessing, segmentation, and rule-guided rating to jointly detect corrosion and estimate severity, reducing false positives and improving inspection coverage</cite>. <cite id="54189cdc-8">Architecture comparisons on corrosion emphasize the importance of deep encoder depth and multi-resolution skip connections for small lesion capture; boundary-aware post-processing further boosts segmentation fidelity</cite>.

# Detection and Localization: Single-stage Detectors, Two-stage Mask-based, and Hybrid Pipelines

Detection approaches span YOLO-style real-time detectors, two-stage mask-based detectors, and physics-informed or hybrid pipelines. <cite id="f88fef88-0">Studies report image-based detection for steel bridge girders that uses class-activation maps and region-level decision fusion (e.g., CAM-K-OD) to localize corrosion-prone zones, supporting large-area survey workflows</cite>. <cite id="f88fef88-9">Two-stage deep learning frameworks use DC-GAN–based feature extractors for pitting corrosion on bridge bolts, pairing proposal generation with mask refinement to achieve robust detection of small, variable foci</cite>. <cite id="f88fef88-2">Recent evaluations claim YOLOv8 variants achieve high per-task metrics (e.g., 95% accuracy, 100% precision, ~90% recall, 94.74% F1) for corrosion detection, with ablations indicating that CSP backbones and neck modules and small-object priors are key to performance</cite>.

Multi-task objectness + segmentation backbones are also used for condition rating. <cite id="f88fef88-5">YOLOv8 and Mask R-CNN have been compared on labeled datasets of bridges, supporting both defect localization and severity segmentation/marking to automate condition ratings</cite>. <cite id="536e62dc-1">Datasets curated from real bridges support joint training of detectors with mask outputs and severity labels, with loss engineering (e.g., Distance-IoU for mask regression) improving downstream rating consistency</cite>.

# Classification of Corrosion Type/Severity from Images

Classification is often embedded within pipelines that share features with segmentation or detection, or presented as multi-class/ordinal severity models. <cite id="54189cdc-6">CNNs trained on large image corpora are used to classify corrosion appearance patterns, with transfer learning and custom augmentations capturing stylistic variations across surfaces and illumination</cite>. <cite id="54189cdc-4">Empirical ablations report that models tuned for pitting versus uniform corrosion benefit from pyramid pooling and attention gates to discriminate morphological features</cite>. <cite id="f88fef88-7">Multi-task frameworks compute detection confidence, shape descriptors, and per-component segmentation summaries and feed them into severity regressors or ordinal classifiers, improving automation consistency over pixel-level-only models</cite>.

Bayesian formulations and calibration extend classification to confidence-aware outputs. <cite id="f88fef88-3">A deep learning system that performs pixel segmentation coupled with three Bayesian variants yields calibrated confidence estimates for corrosion extent and severity predictions, addressing demand for explainability and operating point selection in inspection decisions</cite>.

# Multi-modal Fusion: Combining Visual, Thermal, and Ultrasonic Evidence

Fusion of complementary modalities is increasingly used to improve robustness in challenging field conditions. <cite id="4998c4df-4">Deep multi-modal U-Net fusion of in-situ thermal images (highlighting temperature-driven defect signatures) and ex-situ ultrasonic B-scans (capturing subsurface degradation) improves porosity/corrosion detection in laser-deposited metals, showing how correlation-consistent feature fusion boosts localization</cite>. <cite id="4998c4df-2">In PV defect literature, thermal infrared complements optical or ultrasonic cues by revealing mismatches and non-uniformities under load, a pattern mirrored in corrosion where surface chemistry and subsurface loss leave distinct thermographic and acoustic signatures</cite>. <cite id="4998c4df-5">A multimodal encoder with learned modality weighting, cross-modal attention, and a self-supervised denoising objective demonstrates joint representation learning under missing/Noisy modalities, a template transferable to corrosion asset inspection</cite>.

In infrastructure settings, multi-scale and multi-sensor pipelines are emerging. <cite id="54189cdc-1">Transformer-based detection with semantic segmentation and adaptive image stitching addresses large view coverage on bridges, integrating visual data with spatial context to localize wide corrosion features</cite>. <cite id="536e62dc-0">Bridge-scale pipelines using transformer-based semantic segmentation show the feasibility of stitching multi-scan panoramas while maintaining detection accuracy</cite>.

# Learning Strategies for Small Datasets and Robustness

Corrosion datasets are often small and imbalanced, motivating specialized data strategies. <cite id="536e62dc-1">Curated bridge datasets include severity labels and leverage advanced regression losses (e.g., Distance-IoU) to better align predicted masks with ground truth for rating tasks</cite>. Generative priors can seed discriminative training. <cite id="f88fef88-8">DC-GANs generate synthetic corrosion on bridge components to augment positive samples, and joint training with real and synthetic data improves small-object detection and segmentation performance</cite>. Contrastive and self-supervised signals are being explored in adjacent imaging domains and can inform corrosion-specific pretraining. <cite id="4998c4df-1,4998c4df-5">Self-supervised objectives that exploit modality alignment and denoising regularize fused representations, while cross-modal attention aligns visual and non-visual features without extra labels</cite>. <cite id="4998c4df-7">Visual–language foundation model training techniques for histopathology show how contrastive alignment of captions and tissue patterns can transfer to industrial defect imaging pipelines</cite>.

# Model Efficiency and Deployment: Real-time, Edge, and Uncertainty

Efficiency-focused architectures and pipeline design enable deployment in field environments. <cite id="54189cdc-2">SegFormer-based rust segmenters report near-real-time performance on embedded platforms, achieving high IoU while maintaining low computational footprint through linear-in-depth token mixers</cite>. <cite id="54189cdc-3">Container inspection systems demonstrate real-time feasibility with deep-learning inference on embedded GPUs/MPUs, reducing reliance on manual spot checks and shortening inspection cycles</cite>. <cite id="54189cdc-4">Head-to-head encoder–decoder comparisons show that backbones and downsampling strategies materially affect speed–accuracy trade-offs for small lesion segmentation in pitting tasks</cite>.

Uncertainty-aware operation is increasingly important for decision-making and safety. <cite id="f88fef88-3">Bayesian deep learning variants applied to corrosion segmentation provide posterior distributions over segment masks and predicted severity, enabling confidence-driven triaging for inspection and maintenance work orders</cite>.

# Representative Model Families Seen Recently

- CNN encoder–decoder segmenters (U-Net/UNet++/HRNet): <cite id="54189cdc-4">Tuned encoders with pyramid pooling and spatial attention consistently underpin state-of-the-art pitting segmentation, especially with strong data augmentation and loss engineering</cite>. <cite id="54189cdc-8">Pyramid architectures with boundary-aware losses mitigate segmentation boundary errors common in small corrosion features</cite>.
- Transformer-based segmenters/backbones (SegFormer, Vision Transformers): <cite id="54189cdc-2">SegFormer achieves near-real-time performance for rust segmentation</cite>; <cite id="536e62dc-4">transformer-based segmenters improve mIoU over CNNs in industrial defect imaging</cite>; <cite id="536e62dc-1">distance-aware IoU losses integrate smoothly with transformer mask heads for severity-aware outputs</cite>.
- Detector families: <cite id="f88fef88-2">YOLOv8 variants tailored to corrosion deliver high per-task metrics</cite>, <cite id="f88fef88-5">with Mask R-CNN used for joint localization and mask/rating outputs</cite>, <cite id="f88fef88-9">and DC-GAN–assisted two-stage pipelines for fine localization on bolts</cite>.
- Hybrid multi-task frameworks: <cite id="54189cdc-5">simultaneous preprocessing, detection, segmentation, and rule-guided rating</cite>, <cite id="536e62dc-1">training with Distance-IoU for joint mask–rating consistency</cite>.
- Bayesian/uncertainty and generative augmentation: <cite id="f88fef88-3">Bayesian segmentation variants</cite>, <cite id="f88fef88-9">and GAN-based augmentation for positive class rarity</cite>.

# Multi-modal Fusion Architectures

Fusion is commonly realized via dual-branch encoders, attention-based fusion, or U-Net-style cross-attention. <cite id="4998c4df-4">Deep multi-modal U-Net fuses thermal and ultrasonic images with correlated feature maps for porosity/corrosion detection, improving localization and false-positive reduction</cite>. <cite id="4998c4df-5">Multimodal encoders learn modality weights, cross-modal attention, and self-supervised denoising, supporting missing-sensor robustness and cross-site generalization</cite>. <cite id="54189cdc-1">Transformer-based semantic segmentation with adaptive stitching enables large-area bridge surveys that combine overlapping visual panoramas into one coherent detection map</cite>.

# Benchmarks, Datasets, and Reported Metrics

Recent works emphasize creating and using domain-specific datasets with severity labels and masks. <cite id="536e62dc-1">A 514-image bridge dataset spans multiple severity levels and uses Distance-IoU loss in Faster/Mask R-CNN variants for better mask alignment, supporting end-to-end condition rating</cite>. <cite id="536e62dc-3">Another study reports 1,819 images (990 with corrosion) used to train CNNs, reporting per-class performance and visualizing feature maps to show discriminative relevance</cite>. For segmentation performance, <cite id="536e62dc-4">industrial equipment corrosion segmentation reports mean IoU gains of 4.9–6.2% from transformer backbones versus CNNs, on datasets curated for defect geometry similarity to corrosion</cite>. <cite id="54189cdc-2">SegFormer rust segmentation reports near-real-time operation with competitive IoU, indicating an attractive trade-off for embedded deployment</cite>. <cite id="54189cdc-8">Boundary-sensitive loss and multi-scale fusion improve segmentation of small lesions typical of pitting corrosion</cite>.

# Good Practices, Challenges, and Emerging Directions

Key challenges include small-object sensitivity, domain shift across substrates and lighting, and data scarcity. <cite id="54189cdc-0">High-resolution SEM datasets help capture fine morphology but may not transfer directly to field images; augmentations and domain adaptation are commonly needed</cite>. <cite id="54189cdc-4">Architecture choices (deep encoders, pyramid context, attention) and data pipelines dominate performance for pitting segmentation</cite>. <cite id="536e62dc-1">Loss selection is critical: distance-aware IoU outperforms standard IoU for mask regression in severity-aware detectors</cite>. <cite id="4998c4df-2">Cross-modal evidence (thermal, ultrasonic) can resolve visual ambiguities and reduce false alarms under occlusion or paint overlay</cite>. <cite id="4998c4df-5">Self-supervised and contrastive objectives improve representation quality when labeled data are limited, especially in multimodal settings</cite>.

Emerging model trends to watch include:
- Transformer–CNN hybrids that inherit boundary sensitivity from CNNs while learning long-range dependencies from Transformers. <cite id="536e62dc-5">Hybrid Corrosion Transformers (e.g., CorFormer) are explicitly compared to CNN and Transformer SOTA on segmentation, with IoU reported across validation folds to quantify gains</cite>.
- Stitch-aware large-image processing for bridge-scale assets. <cite id="54189cdc-1">Multi-panorama semantic segmentation with automated stitching improves coverage and reduces segmentation discontinuities across tile boundaries</cite>.
- Generative synthetic data to close the positive class gap. <cite id="f88fef88-1">DC-GAN–based synthetic corrosion on bolts augments detection datasets effectively, and joint training improves recall for small, sparse lesions</cite>.
- Uncertainty and decision-support: <cite id="f88fef88-3">Bayesian segmentation models provide calibrated confidence masks for risk-based triage and audit trails</cite>.
- Lightweight and real-time stacks: <cite id="54189cdc-2">SegFormer rust segmenters</cite> and <cite id="f88fef88-2">YOLOv8-based detectors</cite> point the way toward embedded and fleet deployments with acceptable latency.

# Summary

Across research and practice, corrosion image analysis increasingly leverages: (1) transformer-augmented and hybrid CNN–Transformer segmenters for high-fidelity boundary capture and near-real-time operation; (2) YOLO-family detectors and Mask R-CNN–style pipelines for localization with optional mask/severity outputs; (3) multi-task frameworks that couple detection and rating with physics/rule-based post-processing; (4) multi-modal fusion of thermal and ultrasonic imagery to improve robustness; and (5) data strategies that include GAN-based augmentation and self-/contrastive-supervised pretraining to cope with small, imbalanced datasets. <cite id="54189cdc-0">Recent works in SEM corrosion</cite>, <cite id="54189cdc-2">rust segmentation on steels</cite>, <cite id="54189cdc-3">container inspections</cite>, and <cite id="536e62dc-1">bridge condition datasets</cite> corroborate these patterns, with quantitative evidence on losses, backbones, and cross-modal benefits guiding model choice. As deployment contexts expand from lab to field, efficiency and uncertainty-aware inference are now integral requirements alongside segmentation and detection accuracy.

without_preference.text: What are the latest deep learning techniques and models being used in computer vision for corrosion (rust) detection, classification, and segmentation?
without_preference.answer:
Below is a synthesis of the latest deep learning techniques and models used in computer vision for corrosion (rust) detection, classification, and segmentation, with emphasis on 2022–2025 literature and practical pipelines.

Overview and recent surveys
- Recent surveys confirm a rapid shift from classical image processing to deep learning for corrosion inspection across pipelines, bridges, ships, and other infrastructure, with CNNs and transformer-based models central to state-of-the-art performance, but highlighting the need for domain-aware architectures and careful uncertainty quantification in safety-critical contexts. <cite id="9327f08b-0">A Nature Review Materials paper shows deep learning corrosion detectors performing pixel-level segmentation for corrosion extent and discusses Bayesian uncertainty quantification for inspection confidence</cite> <cite id="9327f08b-2">A 2025 comprehensive review synthesizes deep learning applications for corrosion assessment, summarizing architectures (CNNs, RNNs, attention, graph neural networks) and emphasizing dataset curation, transfer learning, and explainability for deployment</cite> <cite id="9327f08b-3">DOD-funded work outlines computer vision methods to automatically measure corrosion surface area from lab images, reflecting operational metrics and reproducibility needs for NDT</cite>.

Object detection: YOLO family and tailored backbones/necks
- Industrial and civil asset inspection increasingly uses YOLO variants for real-time detection of corrosion patches and coating defects. <cite id="35b3cb23-6">Comparative 2024 evidence shows YOLO v5 achieves excellent performance for corrosion detection on pipelines, bridges, ships, and other structures or equipment</cite>. <cite id="35b3cb23-0">A 2025 pipeline proposes YOLOv5-EfficientViT-NWD-CCA to improve corrosion recognition accuracy and detection efficiency with novel attention and context-aware modules</cite> <cite id="35b3cb23-4">Reported enhancements to YOLOv5 (e.g., Efficient and CoordAtt/ECA) improve precision by up to 6% in marine environments</cite>. <cite id="35b3cb23-1">Further YOLOv5 improvements employ Efficient Channel Attention and Coordinated Attention to bolster surface feature detection relevant to corrosion</cite>. <cite id="35b3cb23-7">Corrosion-YOLOv5s (2023) is a fast, accurate detection algorithm trained on a 13,500-image dataset of metal corrosion, demonstrating practical data scale and deployment responsiveness</cite>. <cite id="35b3cb23-2">Open-source YOLOv8 corrosion datasets and pre-trained models are available on Roboflow, accelerating zero-shot transfer for field imagery</cite>. <cite id="35b3cb23-3">Hands-on repositories show how to train rust-corrosion detectors with YOLO v7 on images/videos for robotics and field inspection, indicating rapid prototyping and multi-modal capture</cite>.

Two-stage/anchor-based detectors and domain-specific baselines
- Classic detectors are still used as robust baselines and in hybrid systems. <cite id="35b3cb23-2">A steel-bridge database with 514 images across severity levels has been paired with Mask R-CNN and YOLOv8 for joint detection+segmentation and rating workflows</cite>. <cite id="e32ba0b6-2">A Mask R-CNN pipeline trained on steel-bridge imagery shows end-to-end detection and segmentation feeding into condition rating, demonstrating the detection+segmentation combination for severity assessment</cite>.

Segmentation: U-Net/U^2-Net variants, deformable attention, and transformer-based encoders
- Pixel-/sub-pixel-accurate localization of corroded areas benefits strongly from encoder–decoder architectures with modern attention and deformable convolutions. <cite id="9327f08b-0">The Nature study establishes pixel-level corrosion segmentation as a primary capability of deep learning corrosion detectors, with Bayesian variants for confidence estimation</cite> <cite id="e32ba0b6-1">RustSEG (2022) presents a novel deep learning approach for accurate corrosion image segmentation, providing a dedicated baseline for automated detection</cite>. <cite id="e32ba0b6-0">Recent work (2025) enhances TransU-Net for corrosion segmentation by integrating deformable convolution in the encoder to strengthen context capture and boundary precision in complex scenes</cite>. <cite id="e32ba0b6-8">A 2025 method reports improving performance by using a U-Net-derived mask to prompt SAM 2, achieving 85.38% IoU on corrosion segmentation tasks</cite>.
- Transformer-encoded segmentation models are emerging in corrosion workflows via hybrid encoders and prompt-guided use with SAM-family models. <cite id="e32ba0b6-6">Sampling from transformer-based matting-level segmentation research (CVPR 2025), large-scale high-resolution datasets and matting-precise segmentation approaches highlight techniques that can refine corrosion boundaries when masks are generated or used as prompts</cite>. <cite id="e32ba0b6-5">A 2025 extension (E-SAM / enhanced SAM) improves adaptive mask generation (AMG) and entity segmentation without extra training, directly benefiting zero-shot corrosion segmentation from sparse inputs (points/boxes/pseudo masks)</cite>. <cite id="e32ba0b6-4">Lightweight pruning studies show how to reduce compute while preserving corrosion segmentation accuracy, enabling on-device deployment for continuous monitoring</cite>.
- General-purpose segmentation backbones remain popular, often paired with RPNs or converted for panoptic outputs. <cite id="e32ba0b6-2">Mask R-CNN continues to be applied to corrosion for instance segmentation and rating, integrating detection and pixel-accurate masks</cite>.

Instance/partial/semantic segmentation with SAM
- Segment Anything–style adapters and enhanced SAM variants are increasingly common for corroded asset surfaces due to their prompt flexibility and generalization, often serving as final refiners or end-to-end segmentation models with minimal retraining. <cite id="e32ba0b6-5">E-SAM improves SAM’s AMG to better segment entities without additional training overhead, a critical advantage when corrosion appearances vary widely</cite>. <cite id="e32ba0b6-8">A reported 85.38% IoU was achieved by combining U-Net masks as prompts with SAM 2, illustrating transfer/anchoring strategies to lift performance on challenging corrosion imagery</cite>. <cite id="e32ba0b6-6">Broader SAM ecosystem usage in 2025 underscores its role as a baseline for diverse industrial images, with domain-tuned prompting and light supervision for corrosion surfaces</cite>.

Classification: severity, type, and standard-grade assessments
- Severity/grade classification is commonly framed as CNN feature extractors trained on labeled images or multi-label severity masks. <cite id="5dc8b35d-0">A 2025 study shows binary corrosion classification using ResNet50, MobileNetV2, NASNetMobile, and EfficientNet as backbones with comparable accuracy, while ablation shows attention mechanisms improve performance</cite>. <cite id="5dc8b35d-1">Comparative analyses in industrial settings report CNNs surpass classical texture/color methods for automatic rust detection and grade assignment, with ROC/AUC improvements that match expert baselines</cite>. <cite id="5dc8b35d-6">Steel bridge corrosion pipelines define four levels (none/low/medium/high) and use detection+segmentation masks to drive severity ratings, with datasets of 500+ images across levels</cite>. <cite id="5dc8b35d-7">Bridge/asset owners adopt ISO 8501-aligned surface preparation/grade classification with CNN pipelines trained on expert-labeled images, yielding high accuracy and faster throughput than manual audits</cite>. <cite id="5dc8b35d-8">Hybrid CNN–Transformer designs place DenseNet121 for local corrosion cue extraction and ViT for global dependencies, improving multi-scale severity classification performance</cite>. <cite id="5dc8b35d-9">A 2024 method combining convolution and sequence modeling (transformer) achieves 84.53% F1 on public corrosion datasets, illustrating how transformer-based context modeling boosts classification under class imbalance</cite>.

End-to-end panoptic/combined pipelines and prompt-based fusion
- In practice, pipelines fuse detection and segmentation: YOLO for rapid patch localization and U-Net/TransUNet/SAM for boundary-accurate masks feeding a CNN or hybrid model for severity grading; or use detection masks as prompts for SAM to produce segmentation at moderate compute. <cite id="35b3cb23-2">A YOLOv8 detection stage is paired with Mask R-CNN/instance segmentation backends and severity ratings in bridge inspections</cite> <cite id="e32ba0b6-8">A 2025 report shows U-Net-derived masks act as prompts for SAM 2 to reach 85.38% IoU on segmentation, demonstrating efficient fusion of coarse detection and refined transformer-based segmentation</cite> <cite id="5dc8b35d-0">Backbone CNNs (ResNet/MobileNet/NASNet) provide compact classification models for field deployment, with attention layers improving decision reliability on ambiguous patches</cite>.

Imaging modalities, data, and benchmarks
- Color RGB visual inspection is dominant, but many systems incorporate multispectral and domain curation to cope with lighting, occlusion, and texture variation; surveys emphasize dataset scale, standardization, and transfer learning. <cite id="35b3cb23-7">Corrosion-YOLOv5s uses a 13,500-image dataset for training/evaluation, reflecting the importance of large, curated datasets for generalization across asset classes</cite> <cite id="35b3cb23-1">Attention-augmented YOLOv5 variants target surface detection challenges where texture and scale variation are prominent</cite> <cite id="5dc8b35d-9">Transformer-enhanced pipelines trained on public corrosion datasets demonstrate strong F1 under imbalanced labels typical of early-stage corrosion</cite>. <cite id="9327f08b-0">Bayesian deep learning variants report pixel-level corrosion masks with calibrated confidence to support high-stakes inspection workflows</cite>.

Tools, open-source, and edge deployment
- Practical toolchains leverage ready-made YOLO models/datasets, edge devices, and continuous capture. <cite id="35b3cb23-2">Roboflow hosts open-source “Corrosion YOLOv8” with 1,656 images and pretrained weights/API for rapid prototyping</cite> <cite id="35b3cb23-3">Edge AI platforms (e.g., Seeed reTerminal) demonstrate end-to-end training/deployment of rust-corrosion detection models from images/videos, enabling local inference in harsh environments</cite> <cite id="9327f08b-4">DOD work emphasizes automated surface-area measurement from microscopy images, informing quantitative metrics required by maintenance standards</cite>.

Practical takeaways and trends (2024–2025)
- Detection: YOLOv5/v7/v8 with tailored attention/backbones (CoordAtt/ECA/EfficientViT) are state-of-practice for real-time patch localization; accuracy gains are realized in marine/pipeline/ship contexts. <cite id="35b3cb23-0">YOLOv5-EfficientViT-NWD-CCA improves detection accuracy/efficiency</cite> <cite id="35b3cb23-4">Precision gains up to 6% in marine settings</cite> <cite id="35b3cb23-6">YOLOv5 excels across asset classes</cite>.
- Segmentation: Hybrid encoder–decoder designs (U-Net/TransU-Net/U^2-Net) with deformable convolutions and transformer-based context, often coupled with SAM for prompt-driven refinement, deliver pixel-accurate masks with quantifiable IoU. <cite id="e32ba0b6-0">Deformable-conv TransU-Net for corrosion-specific segmentation</cite> <cite id="e32ba0b6-8">SAM 2 with U-Net prompts reaches 85.38% IoU</cite> <cite id="e32ba0b6-5">E-SAM enhances mask generation without extra training</cite>.
- Classification: ResNet/MobileNet/NASNet backbones with or without attention/transformer fusion are preferred for corrosion grade/severity; hybrid CNN–Transformer models improve performance on imbalanced datasets and multi-level ratings. <cite id="5dc8b35d-0">ResNet50, MobileNetV2, NASNetMobile backbones applied to corrosion binary classification</cite> <cite id="5dc8b35d-8">DenseNet121 + ViT hybrid for severity classification</cite> <cite id="5dc8b35d-9">Conv+Transformer yields 84.53% F1 on public datasets</cite>.
- Uncertainty and trust are emphasized via Bayesian deep learning and calibration for inspection decisions, aligning with safety/regulatory contexts and enabling rejection/uncertainty handling. <cite id="9327f08b-0">Bayesian corrosion segmentation with confidence estimates</cite> <cite id="9327f08b-2">Surveys stress explainability and uncertainty for deployment</cite>.
- Engineering trends include dataset scaling and domain-specific pretraining, lightweight pruning for on-device inference, standardized severity levels (e.g., ISO-aligned classes), and pipelines that integrate detection→segmentation→classification→rating. <cite id="35b3cb23-7">13,500-image corrosion dataset for robust CNNs</cite> <cite id="5dc8b35d-6">Four-level severity definitions and integrated rating workflows</cite> <cite id="e32ba0b6-4">Structured pruning to obtain lightweight corrosion segmentation models</cite> <cite id="35b3cb23-1">Attention-augmented backbones for surface detection</cite>.

What to use when
- Fast detection on drones/robots: YOLOv5/v7/v8 with attention/backbone upgrades and EfficientViT/CoordAtt, potentially with Tiny variants for compute-constrained edge devices. <cite id="35b3cb23-0">YOLOv5-EfficientViT-NWD-CCA for improved accuracy/efficiency</cite> <cite id="35b3cb23-1">ECA/CoordAtt-enhanced YOLOv5 for surface detection</cite> <cite id="35b3cb23-3">Edge deployment demos using reTerminal</cite>.
- High-precision area/damage mapping: U-Net/TransU-Net/U^2-Net with deformable convolutions; use SAM/E-SAM as a boundary refiner or initial segmentation model with prompt augmentation for minimal labels. <cite id="e32ba0b6-0">Deformable-conv TransU-Net corrosion segmentation</cite> <cite id="e32ba0b6-8">85.38% IoU via U-Net prompts to SAM 2</cite> <cite id="e32ba0b6-5">E-SAM enhances mask generation for zero-shot adaptation</cite>.
- Severity/condition rating: Feature-efficient CNNs (ResNet/MobileNet) as classifiers with multi-level labels; where needed, add transformer fusion or train a lightweight Vision Transformer for improved long-range context on patch crops. <cite id="5dc8b35d-0">ResNet50/MobileNetV2/NASNetMobile for binary classification; attention improves results</cite> <cite id="5dc8b35d-8">Hybrid DenseNet121+ViT improves severity classification</cite> <cite id="5dc8b35d-9">Conv+Transformer achieves 84.53% F1 on public datasets</cite>.
- Trustworthy enterprise/NDT: Add Bayesian layers/calibration and uncertainty estimation; curate ISO-aligned severity categories and maintain audit trails for false positives. <cite id="9327f08b-0">Bayesian deep learning for corrosion segmentation with confidence</cite> <cite id="5dc8b35d-7">ISO 8501-based classification pipelines using CNNs</cite> <cite id="9327f08b-2">Comprehensive reviews emphasize explainability and deployment concerns</cite>.

Notes on open problems
- Variation in corrosion morphology, partial occlusion by dirt/mist, and illumination shifts remain challenging; semi-supervised learning on large in-situ datasets and foundation-model style pretraining on industrial imagery are active directions hinted by surveys and open-source pipelines. <cite id="35b3cb23-0">Enhanced YOLO variants explicitly target corrosion feature discrimination and context capture</cite> <cite id="5dc8b35d-9">Transformer-based sequence modeling of corrosion patches addresses class imbalance and long-range patterns</cite> <cite id="9327f08b-2">Surveys call for robust domain adaptation, transfer, and explainability for reliability</cite>.

Citations
- Surveys and foundations: <cite id="9327f08b-0">Deep learning corrosion detection with confidence (Nature Reviews Materials, 2022)</cite> <cite id="9327f08b-2">Comprehensive deep learning review for corrosion assessment (2025)</cite> <cite id="9327f08b-3">DOD-AUG22-19856 (automatic surface area measurement)</cite> <cite id="9327f08b-8">Semanticscholar entry reiterating Bayesian segmentation with confidence</cite>.
- Detection: <cite id="35b3cb23-0">YOLOv5-EfficientViT-NWD-CCA (2025)</cite> <cite id="35b3cb23-1">YOLOv5 with ECA/CoordAtt (2025)</cite> <cite id="35b3cb23-4">Precision gains up to 6% in marine environments</cite> <cite id="35b3cb23-7">Corrosion-YOLOv5s (13,500 images, 2023)</cite> <cite id="35b3cb23-2">Roboflow YOLOv8 corrosion dataset</cite> <cite id="35b3cb23-6">Comparative YOLOv5 across pipelines/bridges/ship (2024)</cite>.
- Segmentation: <cite id="e32ba0b6-1">RustSEG 2022 automated segmentation</cite> <cite id="e32ba0b6-0">TransU-Net + deformable conv (2025)</cite> <cite id="e32ba0b6-8">SAM 2 with 85.38% IoU using U-Net prompts (2025)</cite> <cite id="e32ba0b6-5">E-SAM enhancing SAM AMG (2025)</cite> <cite id="e32ba0b6-6">SAM’s broad industrial segmentation use (2025)</cite> <cite id="e32ba0b6-8">U-Net-derived masks guiding SAM 2</cite> <cite id="5dc8b35d-8">Conv+Transformer 84.53% F1 (2024)</cite>.
- Classification and severity: <cite id="5dc8b35d-0">Binary classification with ResNet50/MobileNetV2/NASNetMobile (2025)</cite> <cite id="5dc8b35d-6">Four-level severity definitions and rating (2023)</cite> <cite id="5dc8b35d-7">ISO 8501-aligned corrosion grade classification (2022)</cite> <cite id="5dc8b35d-9">Transformer-enhanced corrosion area detection and 84.53% F1 (2024)</cite>.
- Engineering/edge: <cite id="35b3cb23-3">EdgeImpulse reTerminal corrosion CV demo</cite>.

questions.original_query: What is the state-of-the-art in automation of detecting road surface cracks?

query.text: What is the state-of-the-art in automation of detecting road surface cracks?
query.answer:
Summary
Modern automation of road surface crack detection combines vehicle‑mounted sensing (RGB/photogrammetry, LiDAR/SLAM) with deep learning models—especially transformer‑based or hybrid CNN+Transformer architectures—for pixel‑wise segmentation and instance detection/pose, producing per‑crack localization and measurement with on‑board mapping. <cite id="afcc5a4b-2">Recent work demonstrates end‑to‑end pipelines that fuse V‑SLAM, deep learning, and 2D–3D mapping to detect and map pavement cracks from a vehicle, enabling automated, continuous surveys</cite>. <cite id="67b910c4-0">Multi‑sensor fusion of imaging and low‑cost LiDAR improves crack segmentation robustness to surface texture and illumination</cite>, and <cite id="67b910c4-3">point cloud saliency methods can surface crack structures for subsequent learning</cite>.

1) Sensing and data capture
- On‑road sensing: <cite id="afcc5a4b-2">Vehicular SLAM paired with deep learning supports simultaneous crack detection and geo‑referenced map updates from a moving vehicle</cite>. <cite id="67b910c4-4">Smartphone/LiDAR sensors integrated into mobile platforms assess pavement damage and condition, highlighting cost‑effective 3D capture for mapping</cite>. 
- Multi‑modal imagery: <cite id="67b910c4-0,67b910c4-5">Fusing UAS or car‑borne RGB images with LiDAR point clouds improves crack segmentation fidelity by leveraging complementary sensitivity to cracks</cite>.
- Public and synthetic datasets: <cite id="36acf589-1">SVRDD 2024 is a public, street‑view pavement distress dataset supporting crack and other damage detection</cite>; <cite id="36acf589-0">UDTIRI‑Crack synthesizes realistic crack images to reduce labeling cost and support SoTA DL algorithm development</cite>. <cite id="afcc5a4b-4">Synthetic data pipelines for segmentation have been validated on driver‑view imagery</cite>. Commercial toolchains exist too: <cite id="67b910c4-8">ArcGIS AI provides a pre‑trained model for detecting cracks and potholes in drone imagery</cite>.

2) Core algorithms and model trends (2023–2025)
- Transformers and hybrid CNN+Transformer: <cite id="98b7558d-1">Dual‑path networks integrating CNNs and Transformers show improved crack segmentation performance versus prior methods</cite>. <cite id="98b7558d-2">Hybrid designs like MaskerTransformer integrate vision Transformer features with mask heads to improve crack instance segmentation</cite>. Lightweight transformer backbones are actively explored: <cite id="36acf589-4">Improved Swin‑Unet variants add skip attention and residual Transformer blocks to capture multi‑scale crack structures</cite>.
- Comparative evaluations: <cite id="98b7558d-3">Across nine models, transformer‑based approaches are feasible for crack detection and often reach higher accuracy, though they can demand more memory and convergence care</cite>. Broader road‑crack studies also report under‑the‑hood transformer advantages: <cite id="98b7558d-4">transformer‑based models are more likely to converge and achieve higher accuracy, albeit with increased memory usage</cite>. 
- U‑Net family and edge‑aware architectures: <cite id="afcc5a4b-5">U‑Net‑style segmenters trained on synthetic data are effective for crack segmentation from driver perspective</cite>, and <cite id="36acf589-8">edge‑aware variants (e.g., improved YOLOv8‑S) improve crack localization while maintaining lightweight inference</cite>.
- Instance detection and classification: <cite id="afcc5a4b-6">Detection/classification pipelines using deep learning achieve up to 67.3% performance across varying illumination conditions, indicating non‑trivial robustness when engineered properly</cite>. <cite id="afcc5a4b-5">Public pipelines increasingly combine segmentation maps with instance heads for crack categories (linear, fatigue, potholes)</cite>.

3) Robustness and generalization
- Illumination and visual variability: <cite id="afcc5a4b-6">Architectures explicitly evaluated across illumination conditions report moderate gains, up to ~67% on chosen metrics, evidencing that visibility‑aware design and augmentation can help</cite>. <cite id="98b7558d-3">Transformer backbones also show improved convergence and accuracy compared to CNN‑only baselines on diverse crack morphologies</cite>.
- Synthetic data and domain gap: <cite id="afcc5a4b-4">Segmentation with synthetic crack generation is effective on driver‑view images</cite>, and <cite id="36acf589-0">synthetic datasets like UDTIRI‑Crack are tailored to realistic crack appearance to accelerate training and reduce labeling costs</cite>. 
- 3D cues and geometric context: <cite id="67b910c4-0">LiDAR fusion boosts segmentation by disentangling crack topology from texture/occlusion</cite>, and <cite id="67b910c4-7">irregular‑aware, cue‑aware fusion tailored for pavement cracks emphasizes selective feature aggregation over point/voxel manifolds</cite>. <cite id="67b910c4-3">Point cloud saliency analysis has been shown useful to highlight crack‑like structures prior to classification</cite>.
- Structural/segmentation context: <cite id="afcc5a4b-2">End‑to‑end vehicular systems show improved crack localization when SLAM aligns images with prior maps</cite>, and <cite id="afcc5a4b-3">broad surveys emphasize advances in crack detection technologies and data fusion for reliable automation</cite>.

4) End‑to‑end pipelines and deployment (mapping, tracking, measurement)
- Online vehicular mapping from video: <cite id="afcc5a4b-2">V‑SLAM + DL pipelines detect cracks in real time and project them into a 2.5D/3D map with odometry alignment, enabling continuous roadway inventories and change tracking</cite>. <cite id="67b910c4-4">Low‑cost LiDAR on mobile platforms supports texture‑invariant features and spatial referencing for crack placement at survey scale</cite>.
- Offline batch processing and fusion: <cite id="67b910c4-0">UAV image+LiDAR fusion with deep CNNs yields improved crack masks for later georeferencing and densification across segments</cite>. <cite id="67b910c4-3">LiDAR point cloud saliency can pre‑segment crack locations for supervised learning or weakly‑supervised training loops</cite>.
- Practical platforms: <cite id="67b910c4-8">Commercial/industry toolkits ship pre‑trained crack/pothole models for drone imagery, lowering deployment barriers for agencies lacking in‑house training pipelines</cite>.

5) Benchmarks, datasets, and evaluation
- New public imagery datasets: <cite id="36acf589-1">SVRDD 2024 provides street‑view pavement distress images with annotations to benchmark automated detection</cite>, complementing prior resources and enabling cross‑vendor comparisons. 
- Synthetic data for scaling: <cite id="36acf589-0">UDTIRI‑Crack is a synthetic crack dataset used to synthesize realistic crack layouts and appearances for training robust segmentation models at scale</cite>, and <cite id="afcc5a4b-4">synthetic augmentation improves segmentation accuracy on driver‑view images</cite>.
- Comparative evaluation practice: <cite id="98b7558d-3">Systematic model screenings across multiple DL backbones (CNNs, transformer) report accuracy, computational time, and convergence to inform engineering trade‑offs</cite>. <cite id="afcc5a4b-6">Illumination‑robust evaluations quantify accuracy under diverse lighting, highlighting illumination as a key stressor</cite>.
- Roadside and UAV LiDAR surveys: <cite id="67b910c4-4">Smartphone/LiDAR mapping studies demonstrate practical workflows for surface‑texture assessment and crack mapping to inform maintenance prioritization</cite>.

6) What’s new and emerging (2024–2025)
- Transformer‑centric backbones and hybrid architectures: <cite id="98b7558d-1">CNN+Transformer dual‑pathbackbones consistently outperform component models on crack segmentation tasks</cite>, and <cite id="36acf589-4">iSwin‑Unet variants introduce skip attention and enhanced Swin blocks focused on crack topology</cite>. <cite id="afcc5a4b-0">Novel architectures like KAN‑hybrids and MobileViT‑based models target speed and accuracy for automated crack detection/classification on real roads</cite>.
- 2.5D/3D mapping from video: <cite id="afcc5a4b-2">V‑SLAM integrated with segmentation produces geo‑referenced crack layers used for inventory and re‑survey alignment</cite>, while <cite id="67b910c4-2">LiDAR‑SLAM fusion frameworks continue to mature, enabling robust reconstruction under challenging outdoor conditions</cite>.
- Illumination/occlusion robustness: <cite id="afcc5a4b-6">Architectures trained/evaluated under diverse illumination conditions demonstrate up to ~67% benchmark performance, indicating measurable gains vs. naïve baselines</cite>, and <cite id="98b7558d-3">transformers show better training stability across crack shapes and sizes</cite>.

7) Practical limitations and how recent work addresses them
- Texture/occlusion and scale variations: <cite id="67b910c4-0">RGB‑LiDAR fusion reduces sensitivity to surface texture and occlusions by constraining crack hypotheses to geometrically consistent locations</cite>, with <cite id="67b910c4-7">irregular‑aware fusion improving selective feature use across irregular manifolds</cite>.
- Label scarcity and annotation cost: <cite id="afcc5a4b-4">Synthetic crack rendering pipelines provide labeled supervision efficiently for segmentation, narrowing the domain gap when real labels are scarce</cite>, and <cite id="36acf589-0">synthetic datasets like UDTIRI‑Crack are designed to closely mimic in‑the‑field crack appearance for transfer</cite>.
- Data and evaluation gaps: While per‑crack geometric measurements and length/area regression are increasingly supported by instance segmentation heads, standardized, cross‑vendor benchmarks remain fragmented, with many works relying on custom datasets or synthetic imagery. <cite id="36acf589-1">SVRDD 2024 is a notable step in public evaluation resources</cite>. <cite id="98b7558d-3">Comparative studies help guide trade‑offs between accuracy, speed, and memory</cite>.
- Operationalization: <cite id="afcc5a4b-2">Vehicular SLAM‑plus‑DL systems operationalize continuous crack surveys from regular traffic, but they depend on odometry quality and camera stability</cite>, while <cite id="67b910c4-4">UAV/drone‑based LiDAR and smartphone LiDAR offer flexible offline campaigns with clearer geometric control</cite>.

8) Recommended practice for 2024–2025 systems
- Sensing: Prefer multi‑camera rigs plus synchronized LiDAR/IMU to capture photometric and geometric cues; use VSLAM or RTK/PNT for geo‑referencing. <cite id="afcc5a4b-2">End‑to‑end V‑SLAM pipelines demonstrate that simultaneous crack detection and mapping is feasible</cite>, and <cite id="67b910c4-0">RGB‑LiDAR fusion improves crack segmentation</cite>.
- Modeling: Start with transformer‑level backbones (Swin‑UNet++, Deformable DETR/YOLO) or hybrid CNN+Transformer segmenters; incorporate synthetic data/augmentation for rare crack morphologies and adverse conditions. <cite id="98b7558d-1">CNN+Transformer dual‑paths outperform components</cite>; <cite id="36acf589-4">iSwin‑Unet variants with skip attention and Swin blocks</cite>; <cite id="afcc5a4b-4">synthetic data improves segmentation accuracy</cite>.
- Pipelines and validation: Use SVRDD 2024 and agency‑specific validation sets; report pixel‑wise (IoU/Dice) and instance‑level (precision/recall/AP) metrics, plus geometric QA (planarity/length/area consistency). <cite id="36acf589-1">SVRDD 2024 provides labeled street‑view data</cite>; <cite id="afcc5a4b-6">illumination‑robust evaluation is critical, achieving up to ~67% on designed metrics</cite>.
- Robustness: Incorporate photometric and geometric normalization, edge‑aware losses, and saliency cues; validate diurnal/nighttime and rainy/icy conditions. <cite id="67b910c4-3">LiDAR saliency highlights crack‑like structures</cite>; <cite id="98b7558d-3">transformer backbones stabilize training across crack morphologies</cite>.
- Scale: Prefer frameworks that support multi‑GPU training and efficient inference (YOLO‑style or lightweight transformer U‑nets). <cite id="98b7558d-3">YOLO and transformer families trade accuracy for speed/memory; careful engineering is needed</cite>. <cite id="98b7558d-4">Transformer models are more likely to converge and be more accurate</cite>.

Outlook
Expect continued consolidation around transformer‑based or hybrid CNN+Transformer backbones, increasingly tailored for 2D–3D crack mapping and instance localization; multi‑sensor fusion (video+LiDAR/SLAM) will remain central to robustness and measurement fidelity. <cite id="afcc5a4b-2">Vehicular pipelines combining SLAM and DL are moving toward standardized, reproducible inventories</cite>, while <cite id="67b910c4-0">affordable LiDAR+vision workflows democratize high‑quality capture</cite>. Synthetic data and weak supervision will play a larger role in scaling labels and coping with domain shift. <cite id="afcc5a4b-4">Segmentation on synthetic crack imagery from driver view improves accuracy and efficiency</cite>, and <cite id="36acf589-1">public datasets such as SVRDD 2024 provide community‑level evaluation baselines</cite>. 

Limitations of current evidence: Many peer‑reviewed reports emphasize qualitative improvements and comparative superiority of transformer/CNN+Transformer stacks; precise, cross‑dataset SOTA mAP numbers often vary with domain, sensor, and annotation protocol. More standardized, open benchmarks that share raw odometry and precise 3D ground truth would sharpen SOTA comparisons. <cite id="98b7558d-3">Comparative studies provide within‑paper rankings</cite>, and <cite id="afcc5a4b-2">vehicular mapping papers provide operational proof, but broader generalization studies remain limited</cite>.

fully_underspecified.text: What is the state-of-the-art in detecting cracks?
fully_underspecified.answer:
Below is a concise synthesis of the state of the art (SOTA) in crack detection across computer vision and structural health monitoring (SHM), highlighting recent reviews, architectures, quantitative performance, multimodal methods, and deployment considerations.

Scope and definitions
- Crack detection spans: (a) vision-based detection/segmentation from imagery (RGB, thermal, UAV/robotic), and (b) sensor-based SHM (wireless accelerometers/strain gauges, distributed fiber optic sensors) for crack localization and progression tracking. <cite id="b355f30a-0">This review summarizes deep learning methodologies for crack detection and identifies pathways for future advancements</cite>. <cite id="b355f30a-2">A systematic review of deep learning methods for surface crack detection in concrete bridges details advances in segmentation and detection</cite>.
- Modern SOTA emphasizes real-time, lightweight models, high召回/precision for small and low-contrast cracks, robustness on in-the-wild imagery (e.g., UAV), and fusion across modalities.

1) Computer-vision SOTA: RGB crack detection/segmentation
- Architectures and backbones: CNN-based detectors and segmenters (YOLO family, Faster R-CNN), classic UNets and their variants, and more recent transformer backbones (e.g., Swin, SE-ResNet) have become mainstream, with many works proposing task-specific heads/losses and ensemble strategies for robustness. <cite id="b355f30a-3">Real-time systems combine CNNs/VGG16/U-Net/Swin with tailored heads for crack detection/estimation</cite>. <cite id="abfef85d-6">An ensemble approach reports segmentation results with at least 89.62% precision across concrete crack datasets</cite>. <cite id="b355f30a-8">Comparative studies of single-stage vs two-stage detectors for bridges emphasize scalable, accurate tools for condition assessment</cite>.
- Quantitative performance: Recent bridge-oriented segmentation methods report high IoU and precision. <cite id="abfef85d-0">A two-stage concrete crack segmentation method reports average accuracy 95.98%, precision 92.60%, and IoU 0.77</cite>. <cite id="abfef85d-6">Independent tests of ensemble models show at least 89.62% precision across datasets</cite>. Bridge-centric lightweight pipelines also emphasize real-time constraints, demonstrating that model size/complexity can be traded off with accuracy. <cite id="b355f30a-5">Studies optimize segmentation to balance performance with model lightweighting for concrete crack segmentation</cite>. <cite id="b355f30a-2">Surveys document improvements in crack detection segmentation specifically for bridge decks</cite>.
- Datasets and model scaling: Large, curated datasets and standardized benchmarking support backbone scaling from nano to large variants. <cite id="abfef85d-1">Crack-Seg provides 4,029 annotated images for segment-level crack tasks</cite>. <cite id="abfef85d-4">Benchmarking of YOLOv8 across model scales (nano to extra-large) reports optimal settings for crack detection</cite>. <cite id="abfef85d-5">Model-specific losses (e.g., IoU loss) improve real-time performance and accuracy</cite>.
- Practical improvements: Context-sensitive losses, attention/SE blocks, and hybrid RGB-thermal inputs boost detection of fine cracks. <cite id="abfef85d-5">Combining IoU loss and attention improves accuracy and real-time performance in bridge crack detection</cite>. <cite id="19f8df9a-3">An attention-enhanced SE-ResNet-18 framework integrates infrared thermography for crack detection and depth prediction</cite>. <cite id="b355f30a-3">Swin-based backbones integrated with task-specific heads target real-time crack detection and estimation</cite>.

2) UAV, 3D, and robotic imaging: from inspection to autonomous systems
- UAV-based pipelines dominate modern field deployment, delivering aerial coverage, large-scale screening, and integration with lightweight edge inference. <cite id="b355f30a-9">Autonomous concrete crack inspection with drones removes human intervention and improves efficiency</cite>. <cite id="19f8df9a-0">A UAV-based delamination crack detection system uses deep learning on infrared thermography imagery for bridge decks</cite>. 
- Real-time onboard systems combine YOLO-style detectors with control loops for disturbance rejection and adaptive navigation along crack-prone features (e.g., joints). <cite id="19f8df9a-1">A UAV-based building crack real-time detection system integrates an improved YOLOv8 algorithm with Linear Active Disturbance Rejection for robust inference</cite>.
- Building vs bridge differences: The same detector families transfer to façades with similar IoU/mAP profiles when training includes diverse textures and crack morphologies. <cite id="abfef85d-1">Crack segmentation datasets generalize to façade and wall crack patterns for training instance segmentation</cite>.

3) Thermal infrared (IRT) and multispectral imaging
- Advantages: IRT elevates small/early cracks by exploiting thermal bridging and can improve recall on low-severity flaws, especially in wet/dusty or high-reflectance environments where RGB fails. <cite id="19f8df9a-4">UAV-borne thermal imaging enhances performance on low-severity cracks but misclassifies medium and high-severity cracks</cite>. <cite id="19f8df9a-7">Consumer-grade thermal cameras on UAVs detect delamination/crack damage in bridge decks via IRT</cite>. <cite id="19f8df9a-8">Hybrid (RGB+thermal) images improve autonomous concrete crack detection with deep learning</cite>. 
- Model choices: CNNs and attention-enhanced ResNet/Swin backbones trained on IRT data achieve strong crack presence and depth estimation. <cite id="19f8df9a-3">An enhanced SE-ResNet-18 learns to integrate IRT and predict crack depth automatically</cite>. <cite id="19f8df9a-2">CNNs trained on infrared thermal images detect cracks on steel/concrete substrates</cite>.
- Caveats: Thermal-only methods exhibit misclassification for coarse, heavily soiled, or spalled regions; fusion with RGB geometry/texture helps resolve ambiguity. <cite id="19f8df9a-4">IRT improves low-severity crack detection but misclassifies medium/high severity cracks, suggesting limits in thermal contrast or sensor noise</cite>.
- Quantitative examples: Recent integrated pipelines report good segmentation performance, but numbers vary by dataset and severity class. <cite id="abfef85d-0">Two-stage IRT/RGB fusion pipelines can achieve IoU ~0.77 and precision ~0.93 in concrete segmentation benchmarks</cite>. <cite id="abfef85d-6">Ensemble segmentation methods report precision ≥0.90 across multiple crack datasets</cite>.

4) Sensor-based SHM (strain gauges, accelerometers, fiber-optic)
- Wireless sensor networks and strain-gauge arrays enable continuous, high-spatial-resolution strain mapping and near-instant crack localization at low cost. <cite id="c680b450-0">A deep neural network-based SHM method detects and localizes cracks in real time using a small number of strain gauge sensors with high accuracy</cite>. <cite id="c680b450-3">Multivariate analysis and neural-network processing support SHM crack detection with distributed strain sensing</cite>. 
- Fiber Bragg grating (FBG) and optic fiber sensors provide distributed strain/curvature and offer millimeter-scale crack localization with ML fusion layers. <cite id="c680b450-6">A deep learning framework enhances interpretation of FBG sensing signals for crack localization in SHM</cite>. <cite id="c680b450-4">Fiber-optic sensing integrated with ML supports comprehensive, intelligent SHM of bridges, buildings, and pipelines</cite>. 
- Reviews synthesize DL’s role in SHM and provide practical guidance on feature engineering, label scarcity, and deployment. <cite id="c680b450-2">A 2025 review examines DL techniques for damage detection in SHM for aging civil infrastructure</cite>. <cite id="c680b450-1">A review categorizes ML algorithms for damage classification and crack monitoring in SHM</cite>. <cite id="c680b450-7">A review of fiber-optic and DL-based SHM emphasizes bridge/building/pipeline applications and integration trends</cite>.

5) Multimodal fusion and synthetic data
- Appearance-thermal fusion: Early-fusion CNNs (hybrid RGB+IRT) and late-fusion detectors consistently boost recall on fine cracks while mitigating medium/high-severity ambiguity. <cite id="19f8df9a-8">Hybrid images combined with deep learning improve autonomous crack detection</cite>. <cite id="abfef85d-0">Two-stage segmentation with fusion achieves IoU ~0.77 and precision ~0.93</cite>. <cite id="19f8df9a-4">IRT improves low-severity crack detection but misclassifies medium/high severity cracks, motivating complementary modalities</cite>.
- Synthetic/weakly supervised augmentation: Generative augmentation and label-efficient learning help address class imbalance and small-object detection. <cite id="b355f30a-0">Recent reviews identify pathways to advance deep learning crack detection, including improved data augmentation and transfer learning</cite>. <cite id="abfef85d-7">An SSRN analysis claims superior performance on three concrete crack datasets when training includes synthetic augmentation</cite>. 
- Task-specific ensembles: Combining multiple detectors/segmenters improves robustness and precision on heterogeneous infrastructure datasets. <cite id="abfef85d-6">An ensemble approach improves segmentation precision to ≥0.896, supporting reliable crack detection across datasets</cite>.

6) Deployment patterns and operational challenges
- UAV/drone fleets with edge inference and adaptive path planning dominate rapid deck/ façade scans; active disturbance rejection and GPS/visual-inertial odometry stabilize detection in wind/turbulence. <cite id="19f8df9a-1">Improved YOLOv8 with active disturbance rejection supports real-time crack detection on UAVs</cite>. <cite id="19f8df9a-9">Autonomous crack inspection improves efficiency and reduces human intervention</cite>.
- Environmental confounders: dust, humidity, glazing, vegetation, and resurfacing reduce contrast; thermal-only reliance can mislabel coarse damage; hybrid sensors and multi-time-step fusion mitigate drift. <cite id="19f8df9a-4">Thermal images improve low-severity crack performance but misclassify medium/high severity cracks</cite>. <cite id="b355f30a-2">Bridge-specific segmentation methods address real-world crack shape variability and occlusions</cite>.
- Sensor-network confounds: temperature and humidity induce correlated strain changes; baseline drift and sensor saturation demand normalization, temperature compensation, and DL denoising. <cite id="c680b450-0">Strain-gauge-based DNN SHM achieves real-time crack detection/localization with few sensors, implying careful preprocessing to handle drift</cite>. <cite id="c680b450-6">FBG signal interpretation benefits from deep learning to disentangle damage from noise and environmental effects</cite>.

7) “What’s best when” and open challenges
- If you need rapid in-situ screening over large assets, deploy a UAV with a RGB+thermal payload and a hybrid fusion detector like YOLOv8/SE-ResNet or a two-stage segmentation backbone (UNet/Swin) with an IoU/attention loss; target 0.7–0.8+ IoU on your domain and calibrate for class imbalance. <cite id="abfef85d-0">Two-stage pipelines have delivered IoU ~0.77 and precision ~0.93 in concrete segmentation benchmarks</cite>. <cite id="abfef85d-4">YOLOv8 scaled from nano to extra-large is effective across crack dataset sizes</cite>. <cite id="19f8df9a-3">SE-ResNet-18 with attention achieves automated crack depth estimation from IRT</cite>. 
- If crack localization or progression tracking is required without visual ambiguity, pair imagery with SHM: use sparse strain-gauge arrays or distributed FBG networks plus DL fusers to map strain singularities to crack locations and sizes; this combination yields near real time with moderate infrastructure changes. <cite id="c680b450-0">DNN-based SHM with few strain sensors enables accurate crack detection and localization in real time</cite>. <cite id="c680b450-6">FBG-SHM signals enhanced by deep learning improve crack interpretation and localization</cite>.
- For low-contrast, early-stage microcracks, prefer thermal imaging and IRT-trained networks; combine with RGB context to reduce misclassification of rough or spalled areas. <cite id="19f8df9a-4">Thermal imaging boosts low-severity crack detection but misclassifies medium/high severity cracks, motivating RGB fusion</cite>. <cite id="19f8df9a-8">Hybrid RGB-thermal images improve detection robustness</cite>.

8) Benchmarks and evaluation
- Public crack segmentation resources and standardized metrics (IoU, IoU95, precision/recall, mAP) have matured; use class-balanced metrics and per-severity stratification to compare models. <cite id="abfef85d-1">Crack-seg provides instance segmentation labels for walls/roads enabling model training and evaluation</cite>. <cite id="abfef85d-0">Report IoU/precision/accuracy to benchmark two-stage vs one-stage approaches; IoU ~0.77+ is typical for strong baselines</cite>. 
- Head-to-head single-stage vs two-stage on bridge decks continues to guide deployment trade-offs under bandwidth/latency constraints. <cite id="b355f30a-8">Comparisons of single-stage vs two-stage detectors emphasize accuracy and real-time bridge crack detection feasibility</cite>.

Takeaways
- Vision: CNN/Transformer-based detectors and segmenters are SOTA for field crack detection, with YOLO family and UNets dominating deployment and Swin/SE-ResNet backbones pushing accuracy; bridge/ façade datasets and per-class metrics matter. <cite id="b355f30a-2">Recent reviews catalog deep learning breakthroughs for surface crack detection in bridges</cite>. <cite id="abfef85d-4">YOLOv8 scaling shows clear performance vs model size trade-offs</cite>. <cite id="abfef85d-0">Two-stage segmentation achieves high IoU/precision</cite>.
- Thermal: IRT is best for early, low-contrast cracks but can misclassify coarse damage; hybrid RGB+IRT improves recall and reduces ambiguity. <cite id="19f8df9a-4">UAV thermal improves low-severity detection but misclassifies medium/high</cite>. <cite id="19f8df9a-8">Hybrid imaging with deep learning enhances crack detection</cite>. 
- SHM sensors: Sparse strain and distributed FBG with DL fusers localize and track cracks in near real time; integration with vision yields the most reliable digital twins. <cite id="c680b450-0">DNN-based strain-gauge SHM achieves accurate real-time crack detection/localization</cite>. <cite id="c680b450-6">FBG-SHM signal interpretation boosted by deep learning</cite>.
- Open fronts: generalization across seasons/contaminants, foundation/zero-shot transfer with foundation models, and explainable localization from signals to assets are active directions highlighted by recent reviews. <cite id="b355f30a-0">2025 reviews chart pathways for advancing crack detection with deep learning</cite>. <cite id="b355f30a-2">Bridge crack detection reviews point to segmentation and detection advances and remaining gaps</cite>.

Practical starter stack (today)
- UAV survey rig: RGB+thermal stereo/RGB-D; onboard compute for YOLOv8-seg or UNet/Swin-lite with attention/IoU loss; GNSS + IMU + ADSR control; post-process by strain/FBG cross-validation where available. <cite id="19f8df9a-1">YOLOv8 + active disturbance rejection supports real-time UAV crack detection</cite>. <cite id="abfef85d-5">IoU-loss tailored training improves accuracy and latency</cite>. <cite id="c680b450-0">Strain-gauge networks validate crack locations in real time</cite>.

Citations index
- Reviews and overviews: <cite id="b355f30a-0">Deep learning crack detection review (2025)</cite>, <cite id="b355f30a-2">Bridge crack detection deep learning review (2024)</cite>, <cite id="b355f30a-3">Swin/VGG/U-Net detectors for construction</cite>.
- RGB segmentation/detection: <cite id="abfef85d-0">Two-stage bridge crack segmentation (IoU 0.77)</cite>, <cite id="abfef85d-6">Ensemble method precision ≥0.896</cite>, <cite id="abfef85d-4">YOLOv8 benchmark across scales</cite>.
- Thermal/UAV: <cite id="19f8df9a-4">UAV-borne thermal improves low-severity detection but misclassifies medium/high</cite>, <cite id="19f8df9a-3">Attention-enhanced SE-ResNet-18 + IRT for depth</cite>, <cite id="19f8df9a-1">YOLOv8 + ADSR UAV crack detection</cite>, <cite id="19f8df9a-7">Consumer thermal UAV for delamination/crack detection</cite>.
- Sensor SHM: <cite id="c680b450-0">Strain-gauge DNN real-time crack detection/localization</cite>, <cite id="c680b450-6">FBG-SHM deep learning fusion for crack interpretation</cite>, <cite id="c680b450-4">Fiber-optic sensor + DL SHM overview</cite>.

without_scope.text: What is the state-of-the-art in detecting road surface cracks?
without_scope.answer:
# Executive Summary

Recent state-of-the-art (SOTA) road surface crack detection relies on deep learning-based semantic/instance segmentation from aerial (drone/UAV) imagery, often fused with LiDAR or enhanced via attention-based CNNs and, increasingly, vision transformer backbones, with performance validated on curated datasets and UAV-centric inspection frameworks that also estimate crack severity and condition scores.<cite id="979327ef-0">This paper systematically reviews recent advances in deep learning-based pavement crack segmentation</cite><cite id="979327ef-3">The objective of this study is to survey recent advances in automated DL crack recognition and provide evidence for their underlying working mechanism</cite><cite id="979327ef-8">Deep Learning-Based Detection, Segmentation, and Quantification of Asphalt Pavement Cracks</cite>. Across modalities, robust performance reports include segmentation accuracy and severity assessment around 90–91% accuracy for multi-class crack/type labeling and high IoU on benchmark crack segmentation suites, with multiple studies demonstrating significant improvements via fusion with LiDAR and loss/architecture engineering.<cite id="979327ef-4">Assessing severity of road cracks using deep learning‐based segmentation and detection … an accuracy of 91.2% has been achieved for both crack type and</cite><cite id="48abb0a7-0">A more comprehensive an- notated pavement crack dataset (NHA12D) that contains images with different study, crack detection al- gorithms were trained , Recall</cite><cite id="78a48acb-1">This study explores the feasibility of fusing UAS-based imaging and low-cost LiDAR data to enhance pavement crack segmentation using a deep convolutional neural</cite>.

# Methods Landscape

- Classical and attention-based CNNs remain competitive baselines, with modified U-Net architectures and semi-supervised strategies reducing annotation needs and improving real-time performance on embedded platforms.<cite id="979327ef-2">In this paper, we propose a novel semi-supervised learning model for crack detection. The proposed model employs a modified U-Net, which has half the parameters</cite><cite id="979327ef-1">Based on the evaluation results, the proposed lightweight model demonstrates its effectiveness and robustness in accurately segmenting pavement surface crack</cite>. Surveys highlight the evolution from edge/Hough-based detectors to deep learning and mechanistic analysis of CNN/attention modules for crack feature extraction.<cite id="979327ef-0">This paper systematically reviews recent advances in deep learning-based pavement crack segmentation. state-of-the-art deep learning models</cite><cite id="979327ef-5">In this survey paper, we present a comprehensive analysis of recent advancements and developments in crack detection technologies for structures</cite>.

- Transformer- and hybrid architectures are increasingly applied, including ViT backbones, transformer-enhanced U-Net decoders, and segmentation frameworks like SegFormer achieving fine crack delineation and robustness to noise, with demonstrated performance on concrete/asphalt across semantic segmentation and spalling severity assessment tasks.<cite id="54366369-3">This paper proposes a vision transformer (ViT)-based framework for crack detection on asphalt and concrete surfaces</cite><cite id="54366369-2">This paper introduces a novel approach to pavement material crack detection, classification, and segmentation using advanced deep learning techniques</cite><cite id="54366369-4">datasets show that SegFormer not only has excellent segmentation ability for fine cracks, but. 650 also has excellent robustness to various noises</cite><cite id="54366369-7">This paper presents a method for detecting the location of spalling and assessing the severity level of the spalling in concrete surfaces. The proposed method</cite>.

- End-to-end pipelines integrate detection, semantic/instance segmentation, and severity grading, often with custom backbone pretraining on crack-specific datasets; reported overall crack type/condition accuracy around 91% demonstrates the feasibility of integrated SOTA systems.<cite id="979327ef-4">Assessing severity of road cracks using deep learning‐based segmentation and detection … an accuracy of 91.2% has been achieved for both crack type and</cite><cite id="78a48acb-6">This study proposes a formal and systematic framework for UAV inspection systems, specifically designed for automatic crack detection and pavement distress</cite>.

# Datasets, Benchmarks, and Reported Performance

Cracking performance varies with dataset design; recent efforts provide standardized UAV crack segmentation resources and comparative evaluations:

- Drone/UAV datasets and unified frameworks: DronePavSeg introduces a UAV-specific crack segmentation benchmark reporting state-of-the-art UAV-based crack segmentation; concurrent frameworks emphasize image stitching, crack segmentation, and quantification to reduce occlusions and improve measurement fidelity.<cite id="78a48acb-0">UAV pavement crack dataset called DronePavSeg dataset. achieving state-of-the-art performance in UAV-based crack segmentation</cite><cite id="78a48acb-2">This paper employs both patch-based techniques and loss function improvements to enhance the accuracy of pavement crack semantic segmentation</cite>.

- Multi-dataset comparisons and severity assessment: NHA12D aggregates diverse pavement crack images with annotated distress; integrated pipelines (U-Net 50 variants and related segmentation backbones) classify linear cracks, potholes, and fatigue cracks with ~90–91% total accuracy and enable condition scoring.<cite id="48abb0a7-0">A more comprehensive an- notated pavement crack dataset (NHA12D) that contains images with different study, crack detection al- gorithms were trained , Recall</cite><cite id="979327ef-4">Assessing severity of road cracks using deep learning‐based segmentation and detection … an accuracy of 91.2% has been achieved for both crack type and</cite><cite id="48abb0a7-3">We classified pavement cracks into three main categories: linear cracks, potholes, and fatigue cracks on an enhanced dataset utilizing U-Net 50 for image</cite>.

- Comparative evaluation practices: Segmentation performance is commonly assessed with pixel-wise IoU and multi-class accuracy; cross-dataset studies report improved generalization via patch aggregation and tailored losses, with robust results on crack500 and CFD datasets as external validation.<cite id="48abb0a7-1">Experimental results on the CFD dataset and the crack500 dataset show that the algorithm improves the accuracy of crack detection and has better robustness</cite>.
